messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] The distance of my genetic map doesn't seem correct?
parts:
I would look to see if there are problems in the data. The estimated map is coming out to really large genetic map distances, indicating that adjacent markers are not appearing to be linked to each other.

Karl

On Jun 4, 2018, at 1:51 PM, ziming zhong <zm.zho...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello!

I'm following the r/qtl guide to generate my genetic map from the physical distance of each marker. But what I got in the genetic distance something weird like 0, 5, 10 or so. For example, like the second attached picture, which is the screen print of the .csv file for QTL input. The first column is the chromosome_basepair, second column is the chromosome number and the third column is the genetic distance. I think the genetic distance should have decimals, right? Also when I used plotMap to check the map, as shown in the first attached picture, the map seems quite right but the cM distance is totally wrong, I guess. So where did I do wrong? How can I correct it?

I once used all the same code to generate the genetic map for another population, and the genetic map is fine. But this time I use the code for another population, then it got wrong.

So my code is here:
mydata <- read.cross("csvr","","cross.csv", na.strings=c("-"),genotypes=c("A","B"),alleles=c("A","B"),estimate.map=F,crosstype="haploid")
nm <- est.map(mydata, error.prob=0.001,maxit = 3)
plot(nm)
write.cross(nm,"csv",filestem="Chr3",chr=3)
